scenario.name: Salesforce Security, Mandiant & MITRE — SaaS Connected App OAuth Scope Escalation & Bulk API 2.0 Export Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a giant corporate customer-records library where an employee gets tricked into authorizing an unverified third-party research cart with broad library borrowing powers. Handed a reusable library pass, the intruder orders the library own automated overnight forklift to pack entire customer shelves into downloadable spreadsheet crates and wheels them straight out of the building until librarians revoke the rogue cart pass. In this scenario (T1528, Salesforce Security, Mandiant & MITRE, SaaS Connected App OAuth Scope Escalation & Bulk API 2.0 Export Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: unverified OAuth Connected App Consent, then asynchronous Bulk API 2.0 Query Job Creation, then bulk CSV Result Batch Download. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Unverified OAuth Connected App Consent, then Asynchronous Bulk API 2.0 Query Job Creation, then Bulk CSV Result Batch Download, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on SIEM Event 200 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Unverified OAuth Connected App Consent & Refresh Token Issuance
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1528 - Steal Application Access Token)
stages.description: Lured by a smooth social-engineering call or phishing link, an employee clicks Approve on a disguised external Connected App, silently handing the attacker a renewable OAuth key ring scoped to read and export company CRM records. When an organization permits "All users may self-authorize" on OAuth Connected Apps, an attacker social-engineers a user or uses stolen credentials to authorize a custom Connected App requesting api and refresh_token (offline_access) scopes, logged in OauthToken and LoginHistory (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with EventType=LoginHistory , Remote Access 2.0, ConnectedAppName=DataSync_Connector, GrantedScopes=api, refresh_token , offline_access so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes SELECT UserId, AppName, UseCount, LastUsedDate FROM OauthToken WHERE AppName = 'DataSync_Connector' (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , SELECT UserId, AppName, UseCount, LastUsedDate FROM OauthToken WHERE AppName = so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1528 during "Unverified OAuth Connected App Consent & Refresh Token Issuance" under the database daemon's service account). Next, the follow-up artifact SELECT Application, Status, SourceIp, LoginType FROM LoginHistory WHERE LoginType = 'Remote Access 2.0' runs (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , SELECT Application, Status, SourceIp, LoginType FROM LoginHistory WHERE LoginT so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1528 during "Unverified OAuth Connected App Consent & Refresh Token Issuance" under the database daemon's service account). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ POST /services/oauth2/token (Remote Access 2.0 Connected App: DataSync_Connector) / ⇠#1 ACK 200) from Node ① (#1 External OAuth Client) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Bulk API 2.0 (/jobs/query CRM Objects)).

stages.title: Stage 2: Asynchronous Bulk API 2.0 Query Job Creation (/services/data/v59.0/jobs/query)
stages.subtitle: Collection (T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage / SaaS Repositories)
stages.description: Instead of copying customer index cards slowly one by one where noisy page counters might trigger, the intruder submits a high-speed asynchronous bulk export order asking the CRM engine itself to gather every Account, Contact, and Opportunity record into clean batches. Using the OAuth access token, the client submits a Bulk API 2.0 SOQL query job (POST /services/data/v59.0/jobs/query) with operation="query" across Account, Contact, and Opportunity tables, recorded in Salesforce BulkApi2EventLog (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with EventLogType=BulkApi2 , EventLogFile, TargetEntity=Contact , 85,400 rows, BulkJobId=7508c000008AbCd so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes SELECT Id, EventType, LogDate FROM EventLogFile WHERE EventType IN ('BulkApi2', 'RestApi', 'ReportExport') (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , SELECT Id, EventType, LogDate FROM EventLogFile WHERE EventType IN , 'BulkApi2 so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1530 during "Asynchronous Bulk API 2.0 Query Job Creation , /services/data/v59.0/jobs/query" under the database daemon's service account). Next, the follow-up artifact SELECT Id, Operation, Object, CreatedById, NumberRecordsProcessed FROM AsyncApexJob runs (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , SELECT Id, Operation, Object, CreatedById, NumberRecordsProcessed FROM AsyncAp so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1530 during "Asynchronous Bulk API 2.0 Query Job Creation , /services/data/v59.0/jobs/query" under the database daemon's service account). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ POST /services/data/v59.0/jobs/query (SELECT Id,Name,Email,Phone FROM Contact) / ⇠#2 ACK 200) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Salesforce OAuth /services/oauth2/token), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Bulk API 2.0 (/jobs/query CRM Objects)).

stages.title: Stage 3: Bulk CSV Result Batch Download (/jobs/query/<id>/results) & OauthToken Revocation
stages.subtitle: Exfiltration (T1567 - Exfiltration Over Web Service)
stages.description: As soon as the bulk forklift signals the crates are ready, the intruder pulls down every finished CSV batch straight to external servers, leaving high-volume result-download receipts that guide responders to revoke the rogue Connected App token immediately. Once job state transitions to JobComplete, the client streams CSV batches via GET /services/data/v59.0/jobs/query/7508c000008AbCd/results. Defenders revoke the OauthToken record and enforce IP range restrictions on the Connected App profile (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with ResultDownloadUri=/services/data/v59.0/jobs/query/7508c000008AbCd/results, ResponseSizeBytes=14,820,412 bytes , CSV stream, AnomalyEvent=ApiAnomalyEventStore Triggered so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes SELECT JobId, RecordsProcessed,TotalProcessingTime FROM BulkApiResultEventStore WHERE JobId = '7508c000008AbCd' (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , SELECT JobId, RecordsProcessed,TotalProcessingTime FROM BulkApiResultEventStor so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1567 during "Bulk CSV Result Batch Download , /jobs/query/<id>/results & OauthToken Revocation" under the database daemon's service account). Next, the follow-up artifact DELETE /services/oauth2/revoke?token=<refresh_token> runs (which Transmits a crafted HTTP request , DELETE /services/oauth2/revoke?token=<refresh_token> targeting a web server, reverse proxy, or appliance managem so that triggers the web/appliance vulnerability, authentication bypass, or C2 communication channel , T1567 required to accomplish "Bulk CSV Result Batch Download , /jobs/query/<id>/results & OauthToken Revocation"). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ GET /services/data/v59.0/jobs/query/7508c000008AbCd/results?maxRecords=50000 / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 Salesforce OAuth /services/oauth2/token) to Node ④ (#4 Connected App (api + refresh_token)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Bulk API 2.0 (/jobs/query CRM Objects)).

Enforce Trusted IP Ranges on Connected Apps, set Refresh Token Policy to "Expire refresh token after N hours", and forward Salesforce Shield Real-Time Event Monitoring (ApiAnomalyEventStore) to SIEM.
